top.title: Tuckahoe boots Greenwich football from the Class D state playoffs on final play
top.description: Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett's team saw its season come to an end Friday with a state semifinal loss to Tuckahoe. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - Being in a tight state semifinal game at Middletown High School isn't a new experience for the Greenwich football team. Friday, the Witches found themselves in another tight tussle against Section 1 champion Tuckahoe. The game was tied late and the Tigers displayed a flair for the dramatic, first completing a 22-yard pass down to the Greenwich 10-yard line with four seconds remaining. From there, sophomore kicker Zander Gjeloshaj - who caught the pass to get the Tigers into field goal range - booted a 27-yard field goal as time expired as Tuckahoe registered a thrilling 17-14 victory over the Witches in the Class D state semifinals. "They made some nice plays down the stretch," Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett said. "They had a real good second half. We probably needed to be more than 6-0 at halftime. We dominated. Their defense dominated in the second half." Tuckahoe (8-3), ranked No. 2 in the state, did not score until the fourth quarter and still trailed 14-7 until 6-foot-5 junior tight end Luca DelConte caught a pass along the left sideline, stiff-armed a defender and proceeded to dash for a 64-yard touchdown. The Tigers added the extra-point boot to tie it with 3:55 left. On its ensuing possession, Greenwich reached the Tuckahoe 26-yard line and was stopped on downs with 1:23 left. The Tigers quickly drove down the field and converted a fourth-down pass to Gjeloshaj to set the stage for his game-winning field goal. "It just didn't go our way in the second half," said Greenwich junior Ethan Saunders, who shifted from wingback to quarterback following an injury suffered last week by sophomore quarterback Brett Traver. "It was a crazy game right down to the wire," Friday's result was the Witches' third consecutive painful conclusion at this stage of the state playoffs. Greenwich also fell to Tuckahoe 13-7 in last year's semifinals and dropped a 25-18 decision against Burke Catholic in the 2024 semifinals. "I am a little disappointed for my kids. Seniors, it is tough. It is always tough to say goodbye," Linnett said. "I understand what we have accomplished here. In a couple of days, they will, too." The Witches grabbed a 14-7 lead on a 3-yard Saunders touchdown run with 8:02 remaining. "Not having Brett was a big deal, but Ethan did a great job at quarterback. He made some big throws, and his legs were huge," Linnett said. "We adjusted what we had to do during the week and our kids adjusted well." Key moment The only reception of the game made by Gjeloshaj saw the sophomore catch the ball at around the 18 and work his way forward eight more yards. Justin Gjekaj, Tuckahoe's holder, snared a high snap and Gjeloshaj calmly pounded the ball through the uprights to end the game. top.title: Browns’ Delpit Couldn’t Help Himself From Trolling The Steelers
top.description: Grant Delpit has no chill. The Cleveland Browns defensive back talked to reporters on Friday, and before he finished his media session, he seemingly took a shot at the drama surrounding the Pittsburgh Steelers , one of Cleveland’s AFC North rivals. Delpit, who’s played his entire NFL career so far in Cleveland uniform, ended his talk with reporters with a “1, 2, 3 Browns” statement. Here is that moment as seen in a clip shared by Daryl Ruiter of 92.3 The Fan: Grant Delpit with a “1-2-3 #Browns ” walk off. pic.twitter.com/Ml2eLd0viw — Daryl Ruiter (@RuiterWrongFAN) November 27, 2026 Browns’ Delpit Couldn’t Help Himself From Trolling The Steelers Rodgers (8) throws a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL game against Cleveland at Acrisure Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images On its own, that quote doesn’t seem anything remotely beyond normal. But given the wild drama that unfolded this week concerning Aaron Rodgers and the Steelers, it’s not hard to interpret Delpit’s words as a subtle (and hilarious) shot at Pittsburgh. When Rodgers decided to talk and appear on “The Pat McAfee Show” on Wednesday after Pittsburgh benched him, one of his head-turning comments was a story about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy mistakenly saying “1, 2, 3 Packers” during a Pittsburgh huddle. Delpit is hardly the only one who’s made light of the fallout of Rodgers’ exit from the Steelers, but him being a Brown surely adds some flavor to his joke. Cleveland is coming off a Week 11 bye, so Delpit might also have some extra energy to keep up with the news around the league. top.description: San Diego State junior forward Bailey Barnhard (20) dribbles against Hawaii junior forward Zyriah Price on Friday, November 27, 2026 at the Rainbow Wahine Showdown at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center in Honolulu, Hawaii. Trailing by 7 points inside the final minute, the San Diego State Aztecs missed three consecutive 3-pointer attempts on a possession, which typified a frustrating afternoon in a 71-64 loss to the Hawaii Rainbow Wahine on Friday at Bankoh Arena at Stan Sheriff Center. Junior forward Bailey Barnhard scored 17 points with 12 rebounds, her first career double-double, but SDSU (4-3) missed their first seven shots as Hawaii (2-5) opened with a 12-0 lead they never relinquished. Sophomore guard Bailey Flavell scored a career-high 28 points alongside 6 rebounds and 5 assists for the Rainbow Wahine, and junior center Ritoya Tamilo added 17 points and 6 rebounds. “(Hawaii) made some shots that we weren’t ready for. (Flavell) got hot and we couldn’t really do anything to slow her down, so giving up 28 points to a player, we knew we were going to have our hands full with (Tamilo’s) height…hats off to them, they beat us from the jump,” head coach Stacie Terry-Hutson said. In their second road game of the season, the Aztecs shot under 40% from the field in three of the four quarters, including a frigid fourth which saw the side make just 4-of-19 from the field. Senior guard Eva DeChent, who finished with 12 points before fouling out, and freshman forward Mayenabasi Akpan were the only players other than Barnhard to make a bucket in the final frame. Akpan played 6 of her 13 minutes in the fourth, putting up a tidy 7 points and 3 rebounds in her brief bits of action for the game. Despite falling down by a dozen out of the game, the Aztecs were able to battle back to even in the first quarter with 30 seconds remaining thanks to an 8-0 push. We played hard, I thought we showed some toughness,” Terry-Hutson said. top.title: Steelers cap tumultuous week with 27-5 rout of Broncos
top.description: Pittsburgh's Jalen Ramsey returns an interception for a touchdown in the Steelers' NFL win over the Denver Broncos (Justin K. Aller) The Pittsburgh Steelers shook off the controversy sparked by star quarterback Aaron Rodgers's bitter midweek departure to dominate the Denver Broncos 27-5 in a key NFL clash on Friday. Mason Rudolph stepped in at quarterback and threw for 142 yards and one touchdown to wide receiver DK Metcalf, and the Steelers' defense scored two touchdowns as Pittsburgh ended the Broncos' six-game winning streak. Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt recovered a fumble by Broncos quarterback Bo Nix in the end zone for the Steelers' opening touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey ran a Nix interception back for a TD, Pittsburgh's defense harrying Nix into a series of uncharacteristic mistakes in difficult, rainy conditions. The Steelers remained unbeaten at home, improving to 7-4 as they at least temporarily put the ugly split from four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Rodgers aside. Rodgers, a Super Bowl champion who turns 43 next week, had been benched for the game amid a rift with Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy over the coach's offensive play calling. Rodgers then went on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show" and aired an array of complaints about the coach, alleging McCarthy had fallen asleep in team meetings and suggesting he wasn't fit for the job. Steelers owner Art Rooney II voiced support for McCarthy on Thursday, saying that "insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization." McCarthy and Steelers players had been tight-lipped in their responses in the days before the game, although Metcalf flashed eight fingers in a touchdown celebration interpreted as a reference to Rodgers's number eight. "At the end of the day, it's football, and we have a job to do as professionals to go out there and compete at the highest level and win games," said tight end Pat Freiermuth. "Regardless of the noise, it's our responsibility and our job to block out the noise." Rudolph said he appreciated the support he'd received from teammates after they were all rocked by the week's events. "They all had the same mixed emotions that I did, just shocked at what on earth just happened when you wake up on Wednesday morning," Rudolph said. "After the initial shocks sort of passed through, they just made it known that they were with me, behind me. It wasn't like a throw in the towel, season's over vibe." It was a damaging defeat for Denver, which fell to 8-3 to slip further behind the 10-1 Buffalo Bills in the race for the top seed in the AFC. They are tied with the Kansas City Chiefs atop the AFC West division. McCarthy called it a "special win" after back-to-back defeats that had helped ramp up the tensions within the team. "You look at what's happened the last two weeks, we needed a win. We needed a win, and it was old-fashioned. It was black and blue, downhill, just going after it, staying square, fundamental football." bb/des

top.title: Postgame Reaction: Avalanche Rally From Three-Goal Deficit to Beat Wild in Shootout
top.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What an incredible comeback. The Colorado Avalanche, without Nathan MacKinnon or Martin Necas , erased a three-goal deficit in the final 6:23 of regulation before beating the Minnesota Wild 4-3 in a shootout Friday at Grand Casino Arena. Trailing 3-0 late in the third period, Colorado mounted an improbable comeback to steal two points from the top team in the Central Division. Devon Toews , Artturi Lehkonen , and T.J. Hughes scored to even the game before the end of regulation. Hughes and Lehkonen also added assists. Mackenzie Blackwood made 19 saves, including a relatively quiet third period in which he faced just two shots. He didn’t see a single shot in overtime. Cale Makar provided the lone shootout goal among eight total attempts. It’s arguably the most impressive win of the season for the Avalanche, particularly given the circumstances. Following Wednesday’s victory over the Montreal Canadiens, Taylor Makar was called up to join the team on its road trip. Then, right before puck drop Friday, the Avalanche announced that Necas would miss the game with an upper-body injury . Hughes was promoted to the top line, while the younger Makar slotted into the third line. The Wild, meanwhile, were without Quinn Hughes and looking to rebound from their first regulation loss since Oct. 22. Their 12-0-3 stretch came to an end against the Utah Mammoth. Colorado dug itself an early hole in the first period, with two goals that were largely self-inflicted. First, Joel Eriksson Ek opened the scoring with an impressive individual effort after an Avalanche turnover at their own blue line. Blake Coleman then doubled the lead with a solo effort of his own, beating Blackwood on a shot the Colorado netminder would probably like to have back. The Avalanche didn’t have much going for them in the opening period, and that continued into the second. Their best opportunity came on a Hughes breakaway, but Wild goaltender Jesper Wallstedt came up with the stop. Eriksson Ek added his second of the night later in the period, sending Minnesota into the third with a comfortable 3-0 lead. Even with Colorado outshooting Minnesota early, it was difficult to envision the Avalanche having this kind of comeback in them. Head coach Jared Bednar pulled Blackwood with more than seven minutes remaining, shortly after Parker Kelly and Kirill Kaprizov were assessed matching minors. The resulting power play gave Colorado a 5-on-4 advantage, and Toews made it count. The defenseman scored his 10th goal of the season with just over six minutes remaining to get the comeback started. Colorado pulled Blackwood again, and Minnesota nearly put the game away with an empty-net goal. But Makar came up with a terrific defensive play to prevent it. The Avalanche quickly went the other way, and Makar’s point shot was redirected by Lehkonen to make it 3-2. The goal, Lehkonen’s 17th of the season, came with 3:59 remaining. top.description: Florida Gators head coach Jon Sumrall watches his players from the sidelines. The Florida Gators lead the Florida State Seminoles at the half 10-3 on Friday, Nov. 27, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) TALLAHASSEE, Fla. — Florida delivered more than another rivalry victory Friday afternoon. The Gators also brought Florida State’s season to a painful conclusion. No. 20 Florida defeated Florida State 26-10 at Doak Campbell Stadium, securing its third consecutive victory over the Seminoles. However, the result carried much greater consequences for the home team. Florida State entered the Sunshine State rivalry needing one victory to qualify for a bowl game. Instead, the Seminoles will miss the postseason for the third consecutive season. Meanwhile, Florida celebrated a historic individual milestone and an impressive finish to its first regular season under coach Jon Sumrall. Florida Ends Florida State’s Bowl Hopes The Seminoles entered Friday with a 5-6 record and an opportunity to salvage their season. However, Florida’s defense made that task increasingly difficult. The Gators recorded six sacks, forced seven punts and intercepted Florida State quarterback Ashton Daniels twice. Both interceptions came from defensive back J’Vari Flowers. Florida State struggled to sustain drives, converting just five of its 17 third-down opportunities. The Seminoles also went 1-for-4 on fourth down. Although Florida State finished with more total yards than Florida, the Gators consistently made the plays that mattered most. Consequently, the Seminoles finished their season at 5-7. The result marked Florida State’s third consecutive season without a bowl appearance, extending a frustrating stretch for one of college football’s most recognizable programs. Jadan Baugh Makes Florida History Against Seminoles Florida running back Jadan Baugh entered Friday needing just 20 rushing yards to accomplish a historic milestone. He finished with 77 yards on 19 carries and a touchdown. More importantly, Baugh became the first Florida running back to record consecutive 1,000-yard regular seasons under the program’s official statistical records. The achievement added another chapter to his impressive history against Florida State. Last season, Baugh rushed for 266 yards in Florida’s 40-21 victory over the Seminoles. That performance ranked among the greatest single-game rushing efforts in Florida history. Now, Baugh has another memorable accomplishment against his team’s biggest in-state rival. His 3-yard touchdown run in the first quarter gave Florida an early 7-0 lead. The Gators never trailed. top.title: Masked Ethan Brown shines in Illinois win
top.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Just four days ago, Illinois freshman guard Ethan Brown broke his nose in multiple different places. Two days ago, he got surgery to repair that broken nose, causing many to speculate that he may take some time off to rest and recover. That would not be the case. Friday night, Brown returned to the Illini starting lineup without skipping a beat, playing a key role in the team’s big win over the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers. First and foremost, it was a remarkable efficient night for the young guard from a scoring standpoint. He finished with 22 points while shooting 8-12 from the field, and 4-7 from downtown. He also stuffed the stat sheet, adding eight rebounds and four assists. Like usual, Brown played beyond his years in terms of making winning plays. In one sequence in the first half, he cleaned up a missed shot from Zavier Zens with an offensive rebound and putback on one possession, then dished out a clean pass to a cutting Zvonimir Ivisic for a transition dunk shortly after. Brown has been instrumental through the team’s first eight games, as he leads Illinois in both assists and rebounds, while also being a double-digit scorer on average.

top.title: Bronson Reed (Jermaine Haley) Shockingly Dies At 38
top.description: Bronson Reed died at 38 WWE WWE Superstar Bronson Reed shockingly died at 38 amid a serious kidney issues that led to undisclosed surgery earlier this month following his cameo at WWE Crown Jewel 12026 . After taking a bump off the stage through multiple tables, Reed remained in Saudi Arabia after suffering multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney following a garden-variety Beal toss from rising star Oba Femi. The spot appeared to go as planned, but Reed underwent surgery and recovery following the incident. Bronson Reed was a rising star in WWE, positioned prominently with top heel stable The Vision alongside the deliberate future of WWE in Logan Paul, Austin Theory, Bron Breakker and Paul Heyman, who has churned out countless mentees who became Hall of Famers under his guidance. Reed was known for his fast-paced style despite being a big man, and really excelled when he developed his flying splash finisher otherwise known as the Tsunami. Despite being a basic finisher in the context of 2026 pro wrestling, which is more high-risk than ever, Reed’s theatrical splash was a weekly highlight on WWE programming. The former New Japan Pro Wrestling standout was released by WWE in 2021, an incident which took him by surprise. The former NXT North American champion returned to WWE the following year and went on to reinvent himself as a more svelte big man, dropping over 100 pounds ahead of his 2026 return from injury. After suffering injuries at Crown Jewel, Reed’s surgery was believed to have been a success. “In great news, we are told Bronson Reed has made it back home and is continuing his recovery from surgery. Continued best wishes,” reported Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestleZone .) Reed had previously suffered a fractured talus bone in November 2024 and a torn distal biceps in February 2026. Bronson is survived by his wife, high school sweetheart Paige Haley, and their two children, one of which is on the way. Reed was finally hitting his stride as a legitimate potential main eventer, and similar to fellow international star PAC—who passed away earlier this year—Bronson Reed is gone too soon. top.title: Back-end starter continues to build on underrated San Diego tenure
top.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Vasquez #98 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the first inning at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Randy Vásquez Vásquez was an under-the-radar piece in the blockbuster trade between the Padres and the New York Yankees for superstar Juan Soto. Soto and Trent Grisham were sent to the Bronx, with Michael King being the headliner of the return. At the time, Vásquez had pitched quite well in the big leagues, with a 2.87 ERA in 37 2/3 innings. He blossomed into a back-end rotation piece in San Diego, breaking out in 2025 with a 3.84 ERA over 133 2/3 innings of work. Overall Grade: C+ He started off 2026 even better. Vásquez pitched to a 1.88 ERA through his first five starts and a 2.96 ERA through his first 10 outings. He regressed in June (7.84 ERA, 20.2 IP) before turning in a phenomenal August and September (2.76 ERA, 45.2 IP). Vásquez ended the season with career highs in innings pitched (140.2) and strikeouts (87) along with a career-low 1.27 WHIP. Overall, Vásquez had an incredible 2026 campaign. He built on his breakout in 2025 and pushed himself to become a better pitcher. His underlying metrics in 2025 suggested that most of his success was luck. 2026 proved that it wasn’t all coincidence. The underlying stats still aren’t kind to Vásquez (5.54 xERA, .288 xBA), but he’s managed to prove those stats wrong. There is always a question of whether that success will continue. However, with Vásquez as the only viable starter on the Padres’ current rotation, San Diego seems to trust the right-hander to fill out the back end of their rotation in 2027 and beyond.

nigeria.title: Manhunt launched for killers of NSCDC officer in Benue
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Chairman of Agatu Local Government Area of Benue State, Mr Melvin Ejeh, has vowed to ensure the arrest and prosecution of those responsible for the killing of an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC), Inspector Anyebe Anya. Anya was reportedly killed by armed men who attacked him at his duty post at a checkpoint in Agatu a few days ago. The assailants were also said to have carted away his service rifle after the attack. Ejeh gave the assurance when he visited the deceased officer’s family in Otukpo to commiserate with them, describing Anya as a hardworking, honest and dedicated officer. He vowed that those behind the killing would not escape justice, assuring the bereaved family that efforts were already underway to track down and apprehend the perpetrators. “Those that killed him will not go unpunished. We will get all of them. I knew him personally. He was a very hardworking, honest man who was committed to his work. “The whole community is mourning his death. The people of Agatu are shocked and grieving over his death. “We console his family. He was a committed officer. I can assure you that we will get those involved and they will be brought to justice. There is a hunt for them already. “The entire Agatu people will not rest until he gets justice, that I can assure his family,” the chairman said. Born in The Hague, Netherlands, to a Togolese father and a Nigerian mother, the powerful forward has West African roots. His Nigerian heritage makes him a player of interest to Nigerian football fans, particularly those following the growing number of players of Nigerian descent making waves in European football. However, Emegha has chosen to represent the Netherlands internationally. He made his senior debut against Poland in November 2025, explaining that the Netherlands is his country and that he is proud to be Dutch. Although Nigeria missed out on having him represent the Super Eagles, his progress at Chelsea gives Nigerian fans another reason to follow his career closely. At 23, Emegha has the physical presence, pace and goalscoring instincts to make an impression in English football. nigeria.title: A Weekend For Proof
nigeria.description: INEC tests its systems on Saturday. Opposition leaders face their own test on Monday. Campaign violence makes both exercises more consequential. By Tuesday, Nigerians should have fresh evidence about two institutions seeking their confidence. INEC will have conducted its nationwide mock accreditation and result-upload exercise. Opposition parties will have had their scheduled opportunity to formalise cooperation in Abuja. The first must demonstrate operational readiness. The second must demonstrate an ability to act together. Both approach those tests amid a worsening concern: whether citizens can participate in the campaign safely. Wednesday’s attack on Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) supporters in Benin City, Edo State, confirmed by the police, followed Monday’s deadly violence in Delta. Edo police reported one person injured and ordered an investigation. The attackers’ political affiliations and any sponsors have not been established. That development changes the context of the coming days. Electoral preparation now requires visible progress on protection, accountability and public confidence alongside equipment and political agreements. Saturday: Let The Test Produce Evidence INEC’s mock exercise is scheduled for November 28, from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Nigerian time, in 17,676 selected polling units. It will test accreditation, election devices, and the uploading and viewing of simulated results. Registered voters in the selected units are expected to participate. The most useful outcome would be a public account of performance. How many locations opened on time? How many participants were successfully accredited? Where did devices fail? How long did uploads take? How were exceptions resolved? A rehearsal can reveal problems that announcements cannot. Finding a fault early allows INEC to correct it. Explaining that correction gives citizens a reason to have greater confidence. The exercise also has practical support from state governments. Lagos has cancelled Saturday’s sanitation exercise, while Anambra has postponed its own, to avoid obstructing participation. Those decisions remove an immediate obstacle. The APC says it is untroubled by the proposed gathering. The parties’ task is to define cooperation precisely. Joint election monitoring could be valuable. nigeria.title: Two Nigerians arrested over romance scam in Thailand
nigeria.description: Two Nigerian men have been arrested in Thailand over their alleged links to an international romance scam network targeting victims across Southeast Asia. The suspects, aged 41 and 30, were arrested on November 18 at a condominium in Ban Mai, Pak Kret district, Nonthaburi, following an investigation by Thailand’s Immigration Division 3 and Provincial Police Region 1. According to local media outlet, The Thaiger, undercover police officers disguised themselves as food delivery workers to gain access to the suspects’ apartment. With the help of security guards, the officers approached the condominium and pretended to have a parcel for delivery. When one of the men opened the door, they identified themselves as police officers and moved in to arrest both suspects. A search of the apartment reportedly led to the recovery of laptops and mobile phones containing messages linked to fake online identities posing as US military personnel. Investigators suspect the identities were used to establish romantic relationships with potential victims as part of an international scam operation. Police also reportedly found social media accounts allegedly created to deceive Thai residents. The arrests followed an earlier investigation on November 12, when police detained another Nigerian man, aged 37, at Owl Market in Nonthaburi over suspected links to the same network. Investigators later searched a condominium in Bang Kraso, Mueang Nonthaburi, where suspected members of the group had reportedly stayed. However, the men had left before the search. Police subsequently traced the two suspects to another condominium in the Muang Thong Thani area, where they were believed to have stayed for two to three days before their arrest. The Thaiger reported that both men confessed during questioning. However, the charges publicly reported against them are immigration-related offences, including illegal entry and unauthorised residence. One of the suspects, aged 41, had reportedly overstayed his permitted stay in Thailand by 411 days. Authorities revoked their permission to remain in the country and transferred them to Pak Kret Police Station for further legal proceedings ahead of deportation. The investigation into the suspected romance scam network is ongoing. Thai police have not disclosed the identities of the alleged victims, the amount of money involved or the specific roles the two men allegedly played in the operation. nigeria.title: UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom government has outlined two conditions under which travellers can bring goods into the country without paying customs duty or tax, warning that items outside the permitted categories or allowance limits could attract charges. According to the UK government’s customs guidelines, travellers can bring goods into the country tax-free under two conditions. First condition is personal use. Goods must be intended for the traveller’s own use rather than for commercial purposes or resale. Second condition is gifts. Travellers can also bring goods intended as presents for other people without paying customs duty, provided they remain within the applicable personal allowance. The rules apply to foreign visitors and British residents returning from overseas, regardless of whether the items were purchased from regular shops or duty-free outlets at airports. However, the exemptions are subject to personal allowance limits, which determine the quantity and value of goods travellers can bring into the country without incurring additional charges. The applicable allowance depends on where a traveller is arriving from and whether the destination is Great Britain, comprising England, Scotland and Wales, or Northern Ireland. The government also warned that goods intended for business or resale do not qualify for personal allowances. Such items must be declared to customs regardless of their value or quantity. Travellers are also required to declare goods that exceed their personal allowances or fall under banned and restricted categories before crossing the border. Declarations can be made online up to five days, or 120 hours, before arrival in the UK. The authorities warned that failure to comply with customs regulations could result in the seizure of goods and, in some cases, the vehicle used to transport them. Offenders may also face financial penalties or prosecution. The post UK lists two conditions for bringing goods into country without paying tax appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda
nigeria.description: Trials of an experimental Ebola vaccine launched in Uganda on Friday, while a global NGO said it had bought 1.5 million doses of another candidate, as the race heats up to contain the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. There are currently no vaccines or treatments for the less common Bundibugyo strain of Ebola behind the outbreak in DRC, which has caused more than 5,700 confirmed deaths out of more than 11,000 cases since being declared in May, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). Two experimental vaccines are due to start testing on Monday in the outbreak’s epicentre in eastern DRC, the WHO said, focusing on contacts of cases and people deemed at high risk of infection. But neighbouring Uganda announced it had also launched a trial of one of the vaccines, developed by the US-based Moderna group using the mRNA technology made famous during the Covid pandemic. The Uganda Virus Research Institute described it as “Africa’s first mRNA Phase I clinical trial”, conducted in collaboration with Moderna. It will test 224 healthy volunteers aged between one and 65 to measure its safety and immunity potential. The other potential vaccine is the ChAdOx1 adenoviral vector vaccine developed by India’s Serum Institute and the University of Oxford — which will also begin testing in DRC on Monday. But Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, which brings together government and private donors to help developing countries acquire jabs at affordable prices, is not waiting around. After the Covid-19 pandemic, the alliance set up a new $50 million First Response Fund — under a so-called “No Regrets” approach — to allow it to buy up doses in advance even before they have been fully tested. – Deployment – Gavi signed a purchase commitment this week with the Serum Institute for 1.5 million doses of the ChAdOx1, and plans to have “hundreds of thousands” ready to deploy should the trials prove successful and they are approved by the WHO and DRC government. “We’re investing in it, hoping that the signals will be positive, and if that is the case, we’ll have gained months and months on the deployment,” Emanuele Capobianco, Gavi’s director of global health security, told AFP. He said he hoped for trials to conclude “within the first half of 2027” and even “within the first quarter” in a more optimistic scenario. Gavi also has a stockpile of 500,000 doses of an existing vaccine, Ervebo, used against the Zaire strain of Ebola, which began testing last month to see if it is also effective against Bundibugyo. Despite a long and porous border with eastern DRC, Uganda has successfully contained the virus after receiving some imported cases earlier this year. It was declared Ebola-free in August after registering 20 cases, including two deaths. The post mRNA Ebola vaccine trial launched in Uganda appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: Nigeria set to bid to host maiden U-17 WAFCON
nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigeria is preparing to bid to host the maiden edition of the Under-17 Women’s Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON), as the country seeks to attract more international sporting competitions and strengthen its sports economy. The Director-General of the National Sports Commission (NSC), Bukola Olopade, disclosed this in a video shared on his X handle on Friday, saying Nigeria had already communicated its interest to the Confederation of African Football (CAF). According to Olopade, the country expressed its desire to host the competition during CAF’s General Assembly held in Abuja last weekend. “We have said to CAF that we are desirous of hosting the first Under-17 women’s championship,” he said. He explained that the move forms part of Nigeria’s ambition to move away from what he described as a consuming sports economy towards a productive one, where hosting international events would generate economic benefits for the country. “We don’t want to be a consuming sports economy; rather, we want to be a productive sports economy. We want to attract more international events where the economic impacts will be felt by the people,” Olopade added. CAF’s Executive Committee approved the introduction of the U-17 WAFCON on November 21, with the inaugural tournament scheduled to take place between March and April 2028. Qualifying matches are expected to begin in April 2027. Nigeria’s interest in hosting the competition comes amid discussions about the country’s readiness to stage major international football events. Earlier this week, FIFA President Gianni Infantino said Nigeria was not yet ready to host the men’s FIFA World Cup, although he acknowledged the country’s resources, passion and willingness to stage the competition. Infantino, however, suggested that Nigeria could demonstrate its organisational capacity by hosting smaller international football tournaments before taking on events of greater magnitude. nigeria.description: Hackers have breached Cloud One, the United States Air Force’s flagship cloud computing platform, potentially exposing sensitive military, personnel and logistics data. Three people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the intrusion was discovered within the past month during efforts to upgrade the system, triggering disruptions across the platform. However, the identity of the hackers, the full extent of the breach and whether any data was stolen remain unknown. In a statement to Reuters, the US Air Force declined to discuss the security status of specific networks and systems. It said: “We continuously take prudent measures to protect Department (of the Air Force) information, systems and mission capabilities.” A major military computing platform Launched in 2017, Cloud One was designed as a centralised platform for the Air Force’s information technology needs, bringing together services provided by four major technology companies: Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle and Alphabet. The platform supports dozens of applications, including systems managing personnel records, salaries, logistics and military equipment maintenance. Science Applications International Corporation (SAIC) served as the platform’s prime contractor until 2025, when Leidos took over the contract. nigeria.title: France slips into ‘technical recession’ after GDP revision
nigeria.description: France’s economy has slipped into a technical recession after revised official figures showed that gross domestic product (GDP) contracted in the third quarter, extending the country’s economic decline. The National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies (INSEE) said on Friday that the eurozone’s second-largest economy shrank by 0.2 per cent in the third quarter, revising its initial estimate of a 0.1 per cent contraction. The agency also revised second-quarter growth downwards to 0.02 per cent from zero per cent previously, although the figure was rounded to zero in the headline data. The revisions mean France’s economy has recorded consecutive quarterly contractions since the end of last year, meeting the conventional definition of a technical recession, which is two successive quarters of negative economic growth. The latest figures pose additional challenges for the government as it struggles to rein in the country’s budget deficit, with its target of 0.5 per cent economic growth this year now appearing increasingly difficult to achieve. The minority government is also facing difficulties securing parliamentary approval for its 2027 budget, which seeks to reduce the fiscal deficit from 5.4 per cent of GDP this year to five per cent next year. The budget debate comes five months before France’s presidential election, amid deep divisions in parliament. Reacting to the figures, Finance Minister Roland Lescure called for the speedy adoption of the budget, insisting that the five per cent deficit target was non-negotiable. “We must adopt a budget as soon as possible with a non-negotiable deficit target of 5%. It is imperative that we restore visibility for economic stakeholders,” he said. A breakdown of the third-quarter GDP figures by INSEE showed that weak domestic demand contributed to the contraction. Consumer spending rose by 0.3 per cent, but this was offset by a 0.8 per cent decline in business investment. The rebuilding of business inventories contributed 0.3 percentage points to GDP growth, following a 0.7 percentage-point reduction in the previous quarter. Foreign trade also weighed heavily on economic performance, subtracting 0.6 percentage points from output as exports fell by 1.6 per cent while imports increased by 0.1 per cent. Despite the contraction, the Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy was expected to record moderate growth in the fourth quarter. A small number of networks remain paused for maintenance, which Binance called standard practice and said was unrelated to the hack. The update closes out a month of phased reopenings. Binance confirmed the breach on Oct. 29, saying its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that gave the attacker access to a service container, which was then used to submit unauthorized withdrawals. The world’s largest crypto exchange stopped all customer withdrawals for two days after the theft, Reuters reported . When they first reopened, customers pulled a net $4.7 billion off the platform, Binance said on Nov. 2. Binance covered the losses Binance said on Nov. 12 that it had completed coverage of the affected assets with more than $6.34 billion of company funds. The money came from a partial draw on its Secure Asset Fund for Users, part of its futures insurance fund and its corporate treasury, and the exchange pledged to rebuild SAFU to about $1 billion. Coverage is not the same as recovery. Binance replaced the stolen tokens from its own books, while about $2.85 billion of the stolen funds have been frozen remotely by the companies that issue them. The rest remains in the hands of the attackers. U.S. authorities have blamed North Korean hackers for the theft, which North Korea denies. On Nov. 23, the Justice Department moved to forfeit more than $1.1 billion in USDC that Circle froze, and said the U.S. has helped freeze, seize or return more than $2.9 billion since the attack. Launderers turn to THORChain and coinjoin The unfrozen funds are on the move. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Russia’s VTB Opens Bitcoin Trading as Central Bank Finalizes Crypto Test Russian bank VTB began letting brokerage clients buy and sell bitcoin in its investing app on Friday, a day after the Bank of Russia approved the knowledge test every Russian crypto buyer now has to pass. Starting Nov. 27, clients of VTB’s brokerage can trade cryptocurrencies in the VTB My Investments app, the broker said . For now, the trades happen over the counter rather than on an exchange, and access is limited to qualified investors, the legal term for Russians who meet wealth or experience thresholds, who also pass the new test. “In our model, access to cryptocurrencies will require qualified investor status and passing special testing,” Andrei Yatskov, head of brokerage services at VTB, said . He said the test would appear in the app on Nov. 27 and work like the bank’s existing tests for other instruments. VTB handles the buying, storage and record-keeping itself on Russian infrastructure. To trade, clients need to open a separate digital account at VTB’s digital depository, where the crypto is held, on top of their regular brokerage account. The bank received its digital depository and crypto exchange licenses on Oct. 6. “At the start, we will focus on buying and selling cryptocurrencies, and then we will introduce additional services as regulation develops,” Yatskov said. Eight questions before the first trade The launch came quickly after the regulator moved. On Nov. 26, the Bank of Russia approved the first basic standards for brokers and crypto exchange offices, setting the rules for the test. Every investor has to take it, qualified or not, and it is free. Buyers must answer at least seven of eight questions correctly. The standard lays out eight topic blocks, from regulation, technical basics and information security to stablecoins, low-liquidity coins, address labeling and blocked transactions, and volatility, with one question drawn at random from each. Investors who fail can try once more the same day, with different questions. Brokers are barred from sharing the correct answers with clients or telling them which questions they missed. A passing result stays valid for one year from the test date or the latest trade, whichever comes later. The test was the missing piece for Russian banks. When retail buying became legal on Nov. 17 , T-Bank said it was waiting on a market standard for testing, and VTB said it was waiting on the remaining rules. Under the broker standard, the industry’s self-regulatory organization has three working days after publication to send brokers the answer options and correct answers. Ordinary investors still face tight limits once they pass. Non-qualified buyers can only purchase bitcoin, ether and Tether’s USDT, and no more than 300,000 rubles a year through a single intermediary. SPB Exchange sets Dec. 1 start Exchange trading is next. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine New York Wins $1.37 Billion Judgment Against NovaTech Crypto Ponzi Founders A New York judge has ordered the founders of NovaTech, a cryptocurrency investment scheme that targeted Haitian communities, to pay more than $1.37 billion, closing out the state’s case against a couple who fled the country rather than answer it. Justice Anar Rathod Patel of the New York County Supreme Court signed the order on Nov. 24. It holds Cynthia and Eddy Petion and their companies NovaTech Ltd, NovaTech Advisors and NovaPay jointly liable for $1,367,023,585 in disgorgement and interest. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the win on Wednesday. “Today’s historic judgment finally delivers some semblance of justice for the thousands of New Yorkers who were targeted by this merciless scam,” James said. “NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings.” Where the $1.37 billion figure comes from The award matches what the attorney general’s office asked for in October . The figure starts with the cryptocurrency investors sent to NovaTech’s wallet at payment processor CoinPayments, which totaled about $1.16 billion from August 2019 through May 2023, according to an affirmation filed by the state. Prosecutors subtracted the roughly $26 million NovaTech actually moved to its trading platform, leaving $1.13 billion in principal. Nine percent annual interest from June 2023 through September 2025 added another $232.5 million. NovaTech’s traders lost about $18.2 million of the money they did trade, the filing said. Everything else paid out of the wallet, including so-called returns and recruitment bonuses, came from other investors’ deposits. Cynthia Petion was the only authorized user on the CoinPayments account, and the state says she approved at least $134.5 million in crypto withdrawals to wallets belonging to her and her husband. The judge also ordered the Petions’ earlier venture, AWS Mining, to pay about $1.46 million. Cynthia Petion owes a separate $4.69 million tied to her promotion of that scheme. A NovaTech scheme built on prayer groups AWS Mining sold crypto mining contracts and promised 15% to 20% monthly returns before it collapsed in 2019, according to the attorney general’s office. The Petions then launched NovaTech, falsely marketed it as a registered hedge fund broker and advertised trading profits of about 2% to 4% a week. Promoters recruited through prayer groups, WhatsApp chats and ads in Haitian Creole. More than 11,000 New Yorkers invested, alongside what the state called hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide. NovaTech collapsed in May 2023, and tens of thousands of investors couldn’t withdraw their crypto. The state sued in June 2024. The Petions never answered the complaint. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Trades Near $61,300 as Tech Stock Futures Rally The bitcoin price traded near $61,300 on Friday morning, as tech stock futures jumped ahead of a holiday-shortened session on Wall Street. Bitcoin price is on track for its first weekly gain after seven straight weekly losses, though it is still down about 20% in November. The bitcoin price was up about 1.7% early Friday and set to add 4.8% for the week, Investing.com reported , extending a recovery from a two-year low of $57,325.70 hit earlier in the week. Bitcoin slumped below $57,500 on Wednesday as the Nasdaq sank at the open, before a late rebound in tech shares lifted risk assets. Short sellers helped fuel the bounce. Shorts made up 77% of $84.7 million in bitcoin liquidations over the past day, while futures open interest was little changed. That suggests forced short covering, rather than fresh leverage, supplied much of the lift. Tech futures lead the risk rebound Nasdaq 100 futures rose 2.2% by 6:42 a.m. ET, Reuters reported, as investors returned from Thanksgiving and piled back into battered AI-linked shares. Nvidia gained 3.6% in premarket trading, while AMD climbed 4.4% and Broadcom added 3.4%. S&P 500 futures rose 1.6%, and Dow futures gained 1.3%. “There have been some signs that the tech selloff has stabilised for now, and that risk appetite is returning to markets,” Deutsche Bank analysts said in a note cited by Reuters. The S&P 500 is headed for its best week since April, though it remains on course for its worst November since 2008. Bitcoin price has followed that rebound but lagged it. The major U.S. stock indexes are each up around 4% on the week, and silver jumped about 7% to above $44 an ounce on Friday while gold added 2.5% to above $3,670. Stocks close early at 1 p.m. ET, and the bond market shuts at 2 p.m. Rate hike bets and ETF outflows linger The macro backdrop still weighs on the bitcoin price. Traders are almost fully pricing in a Federal Reserve rate hike in December after data this week showed the economy grew faster than first estimated in the third quarter and inflation accelerated in October, Reuters reported. Third-quarter GDP growth was revised up to 4.3%, and the 10-year Treasury yield slipped to 4.84%. Spot bitcoin ETFs are also still losing cash. The U.S. funds lost $453 million on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of outflows, with BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust accounting for $329.7 million. entertainment.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
entertainment.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Tuckahoe boots Greenwich football from the Class D state playoffs on final play
sports.description: Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett's team saw its season come to an end Friday with a state semifinal loss to Tuckahoe. (Jim Franco/Times Union) MIDDLETOWN - Being in a tight state semifinal game at Middletown High School isn't a new experience for the Greenwich football team. Friday, the Witches found themselves in another tight tussle against Section 1 champion Tuckahoe. The game was tied late and the Tigers displayed a flair for the dramatic, first completing a 22-yard pass down to the Greenwich 10-yard line with four seconds remaining. From there, sophomore kicker Zander Gjeloshaj - who caught the pass to get the Tigers into field goal range - booted a 27-yard field goal as time expired as Tuckahoe registered a thrilling 17-14 victory over the Witches in the Class D state semifinals. "They made some nice plays down the stretch," Greenwich coach Brandon Linnett said. "They had a real good second half. We probably needed to be more than 6-0 at halftime. We dominated. Their defense dominated in the second half." Tuckahoe (8-3), ranked No. 2 in the state, did not score until the fourth quarter and still trailed 14-7 until 6-foot-5 junior tight end Luca DelConte caught a pass along the left sideline, stiff-armed a defender and proceeded to dash for a 64-yard touchdown. The Tigers added the extra-point boot to tie it with 3:55 left. On its ensuing possession, Greenwich reached the Tuckahoe 26-yard line and was stopped on downs with 1:23 left. The Tigers quickly drove down the field and converted a fourth-down pass to Gjeloshaj to set the stage for his game-winning field goal. "It just didn't go our way in the second half," said Greenwich junior Ethan Saunders, who shifted from wingback to quarterback following an injury suffered last week by sophomore quarterback Brett Traver. "It was a crazy game right down to the wire," Friday's result was the Witches' third consecutive painful conclusion at this stage of the state playoffs. Greenwich also fell to Tuckahoe 13-7 in last year's semifinals and dropped a 25-18 decision against Burke Catholic in the 2024 semifinals. "I am a little disappointed for my kids. Seniors, it is tough. It is always tough to say goodbye," Linnett said. "I understand what we have accomplished here. In a couple of days, they will, too." The Witches grabbed a 14-7 lead on a 3-yard Saunders touchdown run with 8:02 remaining. "Not having Brett was a big deal, but Ethan did a great job at quarterback. He made some big throws, and his legs were huge," Linnett said. "We adjusted what we had to do during the week and our kids adjusted well." Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt recovered a fumble by Broncos quarterback Bo Nix in the end zone for the Steelers' opening touchdown, and Jalen Ramsey ran a Nix interception back for a TD, Pittsburgh's defense harrying Nix into a series of uncharacteristic mistakes in difficult, rainy conditions. The Steelers remained unbeaten at home, improving to 7-4 as they at least temporarily put the ugly split from four-time NFL Most Valuable Player Rodgers aside. Rodgers, a Super Bowl champion who turns 43 next week, had been benched for the game amid a rift with Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy over the coach's offensive play calling. Steelers owner Art Rooney II voiced support for McCarthy on Thursday, saying that "insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization." McCarthy and Steelers players had been tight-lipped in their responses in the days before the game, although Metcalf flashed eight fingers in a touchdown celebration interpreted as a reference to Rodgers's number eight. "At the end of the day, it's football, and we have a job to do as professionals to go out there and compete at the highest level and win games," said tight end Pat Freiermuth. "Regardless of the noise, it's our responsibility and our job to block out the noise." Rudolph said he appreciated the support he'd received from teammates after they were all rocked by the week's events. "They all had the same mixed emotions that I did, just shocked at what on earth just happened when you wake up on Wednesday morning," Rudolph said. sports.title: Masked Ethan Brown shines in Illinois win
sports.description: CHAMPAIGN, Ill. — Just four days ago, Illinois freshman guard Ethan Brown broke his nose in multiple different places. Two days ago, he got surgery to repair that broken nose, causing many to speculate that he may take some time off to rest and recover. That would not be the case. Friday night, Brown returned to the Illini starting lineup without skipping a beat, playing a key role in the team’s big win over the Western Kentucky Hilltoppers. First and foremost, it was a remarkable efficient night for the young guard from a scoring standpoint. He finished with 22 points while shooting 8-12 from the field, and 4-7 from downtown. He also stuffed the stat sheet, adding eight rebounds and four assists. Like usual, Brown played beyond his years in terms of making winning plays. In one sequence in the first half, he cleaned up a missed shot from Zavier Zens with an offensive rebound and putback on one possession, then dished out a clean pass to a cutting Zvonimir Ivisic for a transition dunk shortly after. Brown has been instrumental through the team’s first eight games, as he leads Illinois in both assists and rebounds, while also being a double-digit scorer on average.

sports.description: Bronson Reed died at 38 WWE WWE Superstar Bronson Reed shockingly died at 38 amid a serious kidney issues that led to undisclosed surgery earlier this month following his cameo at WWE Crown Jewel 12026 . After taking a bump off the stage through multiple tables, Reed remained in Saudi Arabia after suffering multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney following a garden-variety Beal toss from rising star Oba Femi. The spot appeared to go as planned, but Reed underwent surgery and recovery following the incident. Bronson Reed was a rising star in WWE, positioned prominently with top heel stable The Vision alongside the deliberate future of WWE in Logan Paul, Austin Theory, Bron Breakker and Paul Heyman, who has churned out countless mentees who became Hall of Famers under his guidance. Reed was known for his fast-paced style despite being a big man, and really excelled when he developed his flying splash finisher otherwise known as the Tsunami. Despite being a basic finisher in the context of 2026 pro wrestling, which is more high-risk than ever, Reed’s theatrical splash was a weekly highlight on WWE programming. The former New Japan Pro Wrestling standout was released by WWE in 2021, an incident which took him by surprise. The former NXT North American champion returned to WWE the following year and went on to reinvent himself as a more svelte big man, dropping over 100 pounds ahead of his 2026 return from injury. After suffering injuries at Crown Jewel, Reed’s surgery was believed to have been a success. “In great news, we are told Bronson Reed has made it back home and is continuing his recovery from surgery. Continued best wishes,” reported Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestleZone .) Reed had previously suffered a fractured talus bone in November 2024 and a torn distal biceps in February 2026. Bronson is survived by his wife, high school sweetheart Paige Haley, and their two children, one of which is on the way. Reed was finally hitting his stride as a legitimate potential main eventer, and similar to fellow international star PAC—who passed away earlier this year—Bronson Reed is gone too soon. sports.title: Back-end starter continues to build on underrated San Diego tenure
sports.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Randy Vasquez #98 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Arizona Diamondbacks during the first inning at Petco Park on September 27, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Randy Vásquez Vásquez was an under-the-radar piece in the blockbuster trade between the Padres and the New York Yankees for superstar Juan Soto. Soto and Trent Grisham were sent to the Bronx, with Michael King being the headliner of the return. At the time, Vásquez had pitched quite well in the big leagues, with a 2.87 ERA in 37 2/3 innings. He blossomed into a back-end rotation piece in San Diego, breaking out in 2025 with a 3.84 ERA over 133 2/3 innings of work. Overall Grade: C+ He started off 2026 even better. Vásquez pitched to a 1.88 ERA through his first five starts and a 2.96 ERA through his first 10 outings. He regressed in June (7.84 ERA, 20.2 IP) before turning in a phenomenal August and September (2.76 ERA, 45.2 IP). Vásquez ended the season with career highs in innings pitched (140.2) and strikeouts (87) along with a career-low 1.27 WHIP. Overall, Vásquez had an incredible 2026 campaign. He built on his breakout in 2025 and pushed himself to become a better pitcher. His underlying metrics in 2025 suggested that most of his success was luck. 2026 proved that it wasn’t all coincidence. The underlying stats still aren’t kind to Vásquez (5.54 xERA, .288 xBA), but he’s managed to prove those stats wrong. There is always a question of whether that success will continue. However, with Vásquez as the only viable starter on the Padres’ current rotation, San Diego seems to trust the right-hander to fill out the back end of their rotation in 2027 and beyond.

technology.description: Global smartphone shipments are forecast to fall 14 percent this year and another 6 percent in 2027, with a recovery not expected until 2028. The 2026 outlook has been shaped by sharply rising component costs, particularly for DRAM and NAND flash. As Reg readers will be well aware by now, this has been blamed on the memory manufacturers prioritizing output of high-margin chips to go into AI servers and GPU accelerators, creating a shortage of the mainstream components that are needed for devices like PCs and phones. Vendors have responded by raising prices, reducing memory configurations, and withdrawing lower-cost models. As The Register previously reported , memory costs accounted for almost 60 percent of the total bill of materials in sub-$400 smartphones during Q1 of 2026. For 2027, Counterpoint warns the outlook is for continued tight mobile DRAM supply, further price increases for low-power DDR (LPDDR) memory, and limited evidence to suggest short-term capacity increases. "The 2026 decline was initially expected to mark the low point of the cycle, but the memory situation has remained more restrictive than anticipated," said principal analyst Yang Wang. technology.title: Bill for Birmingham's Oracle debacle reaches £128M
technology.description: Birmingham City Council faces a £128.1 million bill for its disastrous transition from SAP to Oracle – more than six times the original estimate for a project that contributed to its financial collapse. Papers presented to its Audit Committee this week put the combined cost of the original implementation, which went live in 2022, and this year's reimplementation at £128.1 million, against £19.96 million forecast in the 2019 business case [PDF]. The report , from program director Philip Macpherson, said the project's funding allocation had previously reached £157 million. The report said the new Oracle Fusion system went live in August without any priority-one or "showstopper" issues. "The program has now moved into the Post Go Live Support phase where [it] continues to provide extra support but slowly transitions towards 'Business As Usual' operating procedures," the report said. It is an understatement to say the same was not true of the first attempt to move the council's finance, HR, and payroll systems off its legacy R/3 SAP system to more modern software. The first project started in 2019 and was supposed to go live in April 2021, but was delayed by a year. After the council started to use the system in April 2022, it soon became beset by a series of serious problems. Although the council had planned to implement Oracle "out-of-the-box," it created several customizations, including a bank reconciliation system that failed to function properly. The council struggled to understand its cash position and was unable to produce auditable accounts . It has spent more than £5 million on manual workaround labor . The system move also contributed to it becoming effectively bankrupt , an event it failed to foresee due to the malfunctioning finance system. It later emerged that officials ignored a "red" warning prior to the go-live date. They were explicitly told the system could cause late payments, a failure to collect debt, and incorrect accounting if it went live. Officials gave the go-ahead regardless. The council decided to reimplement Oracle from scratch, while running the current system as best it could and implementing off-the-shelf software CivicaPay , now rebranded as Civica Income Management. Despite the apparently trouble-free relaunch, the true cost to the council is likely higher than the projected £128.1 million implementation bill. For a start, the original £19 million budget was supposed to support the software implementation for schools , but that was excluded from the reimplementation. Secondly, the council expected significant savings from moving to Oracle in 2022 through greater efficiency. The 2019 business case booked £27 million in savings from 2019 to 2031, for example. A 2024 analysis by Audit Reform Lab, based at the University of Sheffield, estimated that the disaster's direct and indirect financial impact, including lost savings and deteriorating tax collection, would reach £216.5 million by April 2026. Campaign group Protect the Wild launched the petition last month, calling for a national consultation that would consider whether further expansion should be restricted, paused, or halted until those impacts are properly understood and addressed. The nonprofit says the petition smashed the 10,000 signature threshold above which a government response is required in just three days, and the total stood at over 39,000 as this article was being prepared. technology.title: Europe's AI sovereignty push: Lots of cloud, not much silver lining
technology.description: Europe's IT spending is growing more slowly than the global average, according to Gartner, whose analysts warn that the region's push for tech sovereignty faces commercial and technological obstacles. Gartner forecasts European IT spending of $1.57 trillion in 2027, up 9.9 percent from 2026, compared with worldwide growth of 15 percent to $7.35 trillion. For 2026, it estimates spending growth of 20.7 percent in North America and 13.7 percent in China. "The world seems to be racing towards this AI goal of where the large language model provider is going to be, and the race seems to be between North American-based providers and some Asia Pacific providers," John-David Lovelock, Distinguished VP Analyst at Gartner, told The Register . He said Europe had traditionally trailed in IT uptake. "We saw that happen when global sourcing, cloud, and software as a service all came along. It's down to the pushback against the idea of creative destruction," where new technologies replace old ones. Europe's fastest growing categories are datacenter systems, forecast to grow 29.7 percent in 2027, and infrastructure as a service, at 26.7 percent. Even so, Lovelock does not expect Europe to compete with North America and China on AI investment. "For AI provision, Europe is going to be behind, and there won't be a way to catch up," he said. "The AI datacenters, the large language models, the foundational models, the tools and techniques for building out AI are all being centered outside of Europe, but enterprises don't need to do that. So the question becomes: regardless of where the source of the AI is coming from, can the enterprises actually adopt and use it? In one sense, Europe will be behind in the provision of AI, but it need not be behind in the use." The gap nonetheless complicates Europe's push to reduce its dependence on US technology suppliers. The European Union has introduced new rules to encourage tech buyers to favor sovereign tech over the dominant tech vendors, but Lovelock doubts they will move spending much. "Sovereignty is a wonderful flag that we fly on the front of a building. IT is running in the basement. CIOs are not going to buy a second-best solution that costs more simply because it's sovereign. "They are not going to break any laws, but they are not going to make a decision that puts their company in a worse position at a higher cost. While sovereignty gets [vendors] on the list, it doesn't assure that they get purchased," he told us. Earlier this month, Gartner predicted that by 2029, more than 90 percent of EU organizations will have a digital sovereignty strategy, but argued that a fully sovereign technology stack remains out of reach. "The global technology supply chain is too interconnected, and many critical dependencies cannot be replaced at a commercially viable scale," said Bettina Tratz-Ryan, VP analyst at Gartner. ®
